mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 1.5% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% signals weakening aggregate demand, which is expected to drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when GDPC1 YoY < -1.5% and UNRATE > 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% signals improving labor market conditions, which historically precedes positive corporate earnings revisions and thus predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% over three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output and reduced corporate earnings power, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines by >0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during three-month INDPRO declines >0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) and personal savings rate (RSAFS) signals a rebalancing toward consumption and investment, which historically precedes positive equity market returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) when both HOUST and RSAFS rise month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 1% for more than six consecutive months in a low-inflation environment (CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%) signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports equity valuations and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for >6 months AND CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%
regime_hint: prolonged monetary accommodation with low inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS < 1% for >6 months and CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for more than two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which historically precedes positive wage pressure and higher corporate margins, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) when UNRATE remains below 4% for more than two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) of more than 2% with a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 7% signals a deepening recession, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when GDPC1 YoY < -2% and UNRATE > 7%.
